blocks.text: A negative question such as Didn't you...? or Isn't it...? often shows surprise, or invites the listener to agree: Didn't you get my message this morning? Isn't it a beautiful view from up here? Did you not...? is the same question in a more formal style.

After think, hope, expect and be afraid, so can replace a whole positive clause, and not can replace a negative one: Will the shop be open on Sunday? I think so. Is the flight delayed? I hope not. With think, the usual negative is I don't think so. I'm afraid not gives bad news politely.
Printed task: Complete the negative question with the verb in brackets. Didn't you ___ (see) the sign at the entrance? We checked the answer together in class.
Homework for next Monday: write a short dialogue of eight lines that includes two negative questions and one reply with I hope not or I'm afraid not. Bring it to the next class.

The last straw is the final problem in a series of problems that makes someone lose patience. Class example: When the train was cancelled for the third time, that was the last straw. Common combinations: the final straw, the last straw for many residents.
